text:
maria (support): FYI customer AcmeAI hit a spike and saw a bunch of 429s + 503s for their Dedicated pool. They say the autoscaler didn't bring replicas up for ~70-90s, requests queued, some requests started returning 401s during retry. Opening thread with ticket logs and repro.
james (eng-runtime): Can you paste the exact timestamps and any request IDs? Also which model + pool config (min/max, headroom)?
maria (support): Ticket ID: TKT-4827. Spike at 2026-11-03T14:12:05Z. Model: gpt-medium-quant, pool: ded-f-nyc-4, config: min_replicas=2, max_replicas=20, scale_cpu_headroom=0.2, burst_policy=stepped. Customer says traffic jumped from 2 rps to ~180 rps within 10s.
support-bot: autoscaler_event: 1965432105 SCALE_EVALUATION start, observed_qps=178, desired_replicas=18, current_replicas=2
support-bot: autoscaler_event: 1965432178 SCALE_ACTION attempted 16 -> provisioning queued, 4 succeeded, 12 pending (cloud provider). warmup_probe failures: 7
sophia (eng-platform): :eyes: looks like provisioning/VM warmup is the slow bit. But the warmup_probe failures + a bunch of 401s is odd — could be auth tokens for ephemeral nodes not being provisioned properly.
james (eng-runtime): Can you grab allocator logs near 1965432170-1965432200 and the kube events? Also paste the warmup_probe log snippet. Repro steps please.
maria (support): Repro steps customer provided:
1) Set pool to min=2, max=20
2) Send 10rps for 2m to warm baseline
3) Send sudden burst to 180rps for 30s
Observed: 429s start at ~14:12:10, 503s and queued latencies from 90ms to 6s, autoscaler desired spikes but actual ready replicas grow slowly, then some requests hit 401 during retries.
lucas (customer-success): Customer also noted their billing account showed a short 'suspended' indicator for 2m right after the burst — might be a payment check race with node provisioning? They removed a CC yesterday but fixed it; unsure of timing.
james (eng-runtime): Ok two parallel things to rule out: (A) cloud provider provisioning backlog slowing node readiness (B) auth bootstrap for new nodes failing causing warmup_probe failures and intermittent 401s. We should capture kube events, cloud provider instance logs, and our node-init logs.
support-bot: command run: `redwoodctl events --pool ded-f-nyc-4 --since 1965432090 --until 1965432250` => returned high Pending/FailedScheduling spikes and node-init errors: "kms: token fetch timeout"
sophia (eng-platform): That token fetch timeout aligns with billing/payment being in a transient state — our KMS provider may throttle requests if account flagged. If node-init can't fetch service token, sidecars fail readiness and warmup_probe fails -> counts as failed replica.
maria (support): Customer insists billing page showed green but there was a 2-minute authorization recheck in the backend. Are we rate-limiting KMS calls? Any recent rollout?
james (eng-runtime): No recent rollout. We have a per-account KMS quota. For large scaleups our node-init does N token fetches in parallel; if KMS returns 429 or times out we currently mark node as NotReady until retry. Short term mitigation: increase min_replicas or pre-warm with cache nodes. Longer: add local token caching and exponential backoff for node-init so one KMS hiccup doesn't block many in-parallel nodes.
eng-oncall: Immediate actions I recommend:
- Ask customer to temporarily bump min_replicas to 6 for spikes (reduces cold spin count)
- Enable "pre-provision headroom" (we can do a quick config change to keep 4 warm standby when burst expected)
- Engineering to search node-init logs for KMS 429s and add alert if >5% of node inits fail within 5m
sophia (eng-platform): Also add a guard: if billing/account auth returns transient error, allow node-init to mark ready with limited sidecar functionality and fallback to token-refresh once ready, so traffic isn't blocked. We'll make a patch and backport.
maria (support): I've pinged the customer with temporary steps (bump min_replicas + scheduled pre-warm for next planned burst) and asked them to confirm if billing showed any transient flags. They've accepted the workaround for now.
james (eng-runtime): Follow-ups for us:
- Collect allocator logs + node-init logs (1965432100-1965432400)
- Correlate with cloud provider provisioning latency
- Implement short-term hotspot: reduce parallel KMS calls during scale-ups
- Create a test that simulates KMS transient 429s during large scaleup
maria (support): Thanks all. I'll attach ticket updates and close loop once customer confirms next test. :thumbsup:
lucas (customer-success): I'll schedule a follow-up call with the customer to validate the workaround and coordinate a future pre-warm window.
eng-oncall: Noted. Marking this sev-low until we get repro on internal test. If replication of KMS-induced warmup failures succeeds, escalate to sev-2."
